steps.title: Scope the 8-channel PWM controller and fix the NUM_CH parameterisation
steps.goal: Write the Overview and Parameters sections. Describe up to 8 independent channels, each with edge or center alignment, shadowed PERIOD/DUTY/CENTER, a shared prescaler and registered outputs. State how NUM_CH maps onto the fixed 0x10-stride register map.

spec_evidence.quote: Up to 8 independent PWM channels for motor/LED control.
Changes written by software must never produce a truncated or runt pulse
Outputs: `pwm_out[NUM_CH-1:0]`, must be

decisions.topic: NUM_CH parameter and accesses to unimplemented channel slots
options: NUM_CH parameter 1..8; offsets for channels >= NUM_CH read 0 and ignore writes
Always build 8 channels and leave unused outputs unconnected
decisions.choice: NUM_CH is a synthesis parameter (1..8). Register slots for channels n >= NUM_CH, and any unmapped offset, read as 0 and ignore writes.
decisions.rationale: The spec uses NUM_CH in the port list and says 'up to 8'. The bus has no error response, so read-as-zero is the only consistent behaviour.
decisions.question: With NUM_CH < 8, should register accesses to unimplemented channels read as 0 and ignore writes?

done_when: Overview lists every feature in P2, P6, P9 and P10, including the no-runt guarantee for value updates and the agreed immediate-stop exception for EN/GEN clears.
Parameters table defines NUM_CH (legal range 1..8, default 8) and states that counter width is fixed at 16 bits.
Address-to-channel decoding is stated for all of 0x00 through 0x8C.

steps.title: Register bus decode, register file and one-cycle read path
steps.goal: Define the Interface and the register file: word-aligned decode of reg_addr[7:0], write strobes into the software-visible (preload) CTRL and CHn_* registers, and a registered reg_rdata returned one cycle after reg_rd. Also define which value each readback returns (software-written preload vs active shadow value).

spec_evidence.quote: Simple synchronous register bus, 32-bit, word-aligned:
Read data is returned one cycle after `reg_rd`. No wait states, no error response.
Reserved bits read as 0. All registers reset to 0.
Current counter value.

decisions.topic: Readback value of shadowed registers (PERIOD, DUTY, CENTER)
options: Return the last software-written (preload) value
Return the currently active (shadow) value
decisions.choice: Reads return the last value written by software (the preload), not the value currently in use by the counter.
decisions.rationale: This is the common read-what-you-wrote convention and lets software verify its writes. The active value can be inferred from period boundaries.
decisions.question: When software reads CHn_PERIOD, CHn_DUTY or CHn_CFG.CENTER, should it see the value it last wrote or the value currently in effect?

options: Registered rdata captured on reg_rd; holds the last value otherwise
Registered rdata forced to 0 when no read is in progress
decisions.choice: reg_rdata is a flop loaded when reg_rd=1 and otherwise holds its value. A same-cycle write to the same address returns the pre-write value.
decisions.rationale: Meets the one-cycle latency with minimal logic. The spec does not define a collision case.
decisions.question: When reg_rd and reg_wr hit the same register in the same cycle, should the read return the old value or the newly written value?

done_when: Port table lists clk, rst_n, reg_wr, reg_rd, reg_addr[7:0], reg_wdata[31:0], reg_rdata[31:0] and pwm_out[NUM_CH-1:0], with direction, width and description.
Every register field has defined write behaviour, and reserved bits are masked to 0 on read.
Writes to the RO COUNT register are explicitly ignored.
The handling of reg_addr[1:0] (ignored) is stated.

steps.title: Shared prescaler tick generator driven by CTRL.PRESC
steps.goal: Specify a single prescaler counter that produces a one-cycle tick every PRESC+1 clocks. Define how a PRESC change mid-count is handled and whether the prescaler runs while GEN=0.

spec_evidence.quote: Clock prescaler. Counters advance every PRESC+1 clocks.
Global enable. 0 = all channels stopped.

decisions.topic: Prescaler structure and PRESC update timing
options: One global prescaler; PRESC change takes effect immediately; prescaler held in reset while GEN=0
Per-channel prescaler
PRESC shadowed and loaded at a boundary
decisions.choice: Use one global 16-bit prescaler shared by all channels. It is held at 0 while GEN=0. A PRESC write takes effect immediately against the live PRESC (compare uses >= so lowering PRESC wraps at once); it is not double-buffered.
decisions.rationale: PRESC lives in the global CTRL register and the spec does not list it as shadowed. Changing the tick rate stretches or compresses ticks but cannot create a runt pulse in tick units.
decisions.question: Should a change to CTRL.PRESC take effect immediately, or be buffered until a period boundary like PERIOD/DUTY?

done_when: Tick generation is described so that PRESC=0 gives a tick every clock and PRESC=N gives a tick every N+1 clocks.
Behaviour when PRESC is lowered below the current prescaler count is defined, with no lock-up.
The tick is shown as a single shared signal fanned out to all channel counters.

steps.title: Per-channel 16-bit counter for edge-aligned up-count and center-aligned up/down count
steps.goal: Define the counter sequence in both modes relative to the active PERIOD. Define where the period boundary is in each mode and what CHn_COUNT reports.

spec_evidence.quote: Edge-aligned: output active at start of period, inactive after DUTY ticks.
active pulse is centred in the period; period is twice as long as
edge-aligned for the same PERIOD value (up/down counting).
Period in counter ticks.

options: Count 0..PERIOD-1 (period = PERIOD ticks); PERIOD=0 holds counter at 0
Count 0..PERIOD (period = PERIOD+1 ticks)
decisions.choice: The edge-aligned counter runs 0..PERIOD-1 and wraps, so the period is exactly PERIOD ticks. The boundary is the wrap to 0. With PERIOD=0 the counter holds at 0, every tick is a boundary, and the output follows the DUTY rules (DUTY=0 inactive, otherwise active).
decisions.rationale: 'Period in counter ticks' reads most naturally as exactly PERIOD ticks. PERIOD=0 needs some defined behaviour.
decisions.question: In edge-aligned mode, should PERIOD=N give a period of exactly N ticks (count 0..N-1) or N+1 ticks? And what should happen when PERIOD=0?

decisions.topic: Center-aligned counting sequence and boundary location
options: Triangle 0 up to PERIOD then down to 0 (2*PERIOD ticks); boundary at bottom (count 0); pulse centred at top
Boundary at top with pulse centred at bottom
Load shadows at both top and bottom
decisions.choice: The counter goes up from 0 to PERIOD, then down to 0, giving 2*PERIOD ticks. The period boundary, and therefore the shadow load, occurs only at the bottom (count 0). The output is active while count > PERIOD-DUTY, so the pulse is 2*DUTY ticks wide and centred on the top of the triangle.
decisions.rationale: This gives exactly twice the edge-aligned period and a single boundary per period, matching 'load at the period boundary'. Centring on the top keeps the boundary in an inactive region, so loads cannot cause runts.
decisions.question: In center-aligned mode, should the period boundary (shadow load point) be at counter bottom (0) with the pulse centred at the top, or the reverse, and should loading occur only once per period?

done_when: Cycle-level counter sequences are given for edge-aligned PERIOD=4 and center-aligned PERIOD=4.
Direction-state storage for up/down counting is defined, along with its reset to 0 and its clear to 0 while the channel is stopped.
CHn_COUNT readback is defined in both modes.
The counter advances only on the prescaler tick while the channel runs.

steps.title: Double-buffered PERIOD/DUTY/CENTER shadow load at the period boundary
steps.goal: Define the two-level storage (software preload plus active shadow) for PERIOD, DUTY and CENTER. Define the exact load condition so that no software write produces a truncated or runt pulse, with shadows tracking the preloads continuously while the channel is stopped.

spec_evidence.quote: PERIOD, DUTY and CENTER are double-buffered (shadow registers) and load at the period boundary.
values take effect at the next period boundary.

decisions.topic: Shadow load behaviour when the channel is not running
options: Shadows transparent (load every cycle) while EN=0 or GEN=0; boundary-only loads while running
Shadows only ever load at a boundary, even when stopped
decisions.choice: While the channel is stopped (EN=0 or GEN=0), the shadows continuously track the preloads. While running, they load only at the period boundary. Re-enabling starts a clean period at count 0 with the latest PERIOD, DUTY and CENTER. A CENTER change at a boundary restarts the counter at 0 (dir=0) in the new mode.
decisions.rationale: Settled by the user's answer to Q1: shadows track preloads while stopped so re-enable uses the latest values.

done_when: A load-enable equation is given for each shadow field: load = ~run | boundary.
It is shown that a write landing in the same cycle as a boundary has a defined outcome: either the new value loads or it waits one more period.
A mode switch between edge and center is shown to take effect only at a boundary while running.

steps.title: Compare, polarity and registered glitch-free pwm_out stage
steps.goal: Define the per-channel compare logic, including the DUTY=0 and DUTY>=PERIOD overrides, the POL inversion and the disabled-level forcing. All of this is combined before a single output flop per channel.

spec_evidence.quote: output always inactive. DUTY
output always active.
Output polarity. 0 = active-high, 1 = active-low.
Disabled channel drives its inactive level.
glitch-free (registered).

options: Final flop after compare, override, polarity and enable gating
Register only the compare result and apply polarity combinationally
decisions.choice: Each pwm_out bit comes directly from a flop whose D input combines compare, DUTY overrides, enable gating and POL.
decisions.rationale: P10 requires registered, glitch-free outputs, so no logic may sit after the flop.

done_when: A truth table covers EN/GEN, DUTY=0, DUTY>=PERIOD, normal compare and POL.
The output-flop reset value is stated, and its interaction with POL after reset is noted: with all registers 0, POL=0 and the output is low.
One cycle of latency from counter state to pwm_out is documented.

steps.title: Immediate-stop enable semantics and POL timing against the no-runt rule
steps.goal: Document how GEN and EN start and stop channels per the Q1 answer (immediate stop, counter and dir cleared, fresh period on re-enable), and decide when POL changes apply, since POL is not listed as shadowed but the spec forbids runt pulses from software changes.

spec_evidence.quote: Global enable. 0 = all channels stopped.
Channel enable.
Changes written by software must never produce a truncated or runt pulse

decisions.topic: Enable/disable timing and counter state while stopped
options: Immediate: disable forces inactive and resets counter to 0; enable starts a fresh period at count 0
Disable deferred to the end of the current period (no truncation)
Stop holds counter value and resumes from it
decisions.choice: Clearing EN or GEN takes effect at once: pwm_out goes to its inactive level (the POL value) on the next cycle, possibly truncating the pulse. Counter and dir are cleared to 0 while stopped. Setting EN/GEN starts a clean new period at count 0 with the latest shadowed values.
decisions.rationale: Settled by the user's answer to Q1; the truncation on disable is an accepted exception to the P2 no-runt rule.

options: POL applies immediately (next cycle)
POL shadowed and loaded at the period boundary
decisions.choice: POL is not double-buffered and applies on the next cycle, inverting the current output level.
decisions.rationale: P9 lists only PERIOD, DUTY and CENTER as shadowed. Polarity is normally configured while the channel is stopped; a live change is a configuration change, not a duty update.
decisions.question: If software changes CHn_CFG.POL while the channel is running, should it apply immediately or wait for the next period boundary?

options: Channels with EN=1 all restart at count 0 when GEN rises (phase-aligned); individual EN rising starts that channel independently
Fully free-running and unsynchronised
decisions.choice: All channel counters are cleared while GEN=0, and the prescaler is held at 0, so channels already enabled start in phase when GEN rises. A channel enabled later starts its own period on its EN rise, aligned to the shared tick.
decisions.rationale: This follows from the D6 clear-on-stop behaviour with the shared tick, and gives software a way to phase-align channels for free.
decisions.question: Is there any requirement for channels to be phase-aligned (e.g., all start together when GEN is set), or are they fully independent?

done_when: A run-state definition per channel (run = GEN & EN) and its effect on the counter, dir, shadows and output are written down.
Behaviour for each of the four GEN/EN transitions is tabulated, including the one-cycle stop latency.
The accepted truncation on EN/GEN clear is explicitly called out as the only exception to the P2 no-runt rule, citing the user answer.

steps.title: Clocking and active-low reset strategy for a single 100 MHz domain
steps.goal: Document the single clock domain and the rst_n handling. Confirm that all registers, shadows, counters, the prescaler and the output flops reset to 0, and that the 16-bit compare paths close timing at 100 MHz.

spec_evidence.quote: Clock: `clk` (100 MHz). Reset: `rst_n`, active-low.
Reserved bits read as 0. All registers reset to 0.

options: Asynchronous assert, synchronous deassert (synchronizer external or internal)
Fully synchronous reset
decisions.choice: Use asynchronous active-low reset on all flops. rst_n is assumed already synchronised for deassertion by the SoC.
decisions.rationale: This guarantees pwm_out reaches its inactive level immediately on reset even without a clock, which is common for motor/LED drivers.
decisions.question: Should rst_n be treated as asynchronous (with deassertion already synchronised externally) or as a synchronous reset?

done_when: The reset value is listed for every storage element, including preloads, shadows, the prescaler, counters, direction bits, the rdata flop and the output flops.
The critical path is identified (16-bit compare plus output mux) and is feasible at 10 ns.
The absence of CDC is confirmed.

steps.title: Block diagram and end-to-end timing of write-to-effect and read latency
steps.goal: Assemble the block diagram: bus decode, register file, prescaler, per-channel shadow/counter/compare/output slices and the read mux. Provide the timing diagrams that show the observable latencies.

spec_evidence.quote: Read data is returned one cycle after `reg_rd`.
values take effect at the next period boundary.

done_when: The block diagram shows one shared prescaler and NUM_CH replicated channel slices.
Waveforms show a reg_rd to reg_rdata timing of one cycle.
Waveforms show a DUTY write mid-period that takes effect at the next boundary, in both modes.
Waveforms show the GEN rise to first pwm_out edge latency and the EN clear to inactive-output latency.

steps.title: Corner cases specific to this PWM: degenerate PERIOD/DUTY, mode switch, PRESC change, mid-pulse stop
steps.goal: Enumerate and resolve the edge conditions. None of these return bus errors, because the bus has no error response.

spec_evidence.quote: output always inactive. DUTY
No wait states, no error response.

done_when: Covers PERIOD=0, PERIOD=1, DUTY=PERIOD, DUTY=PERIOD-1 and PERIOD=0xFFFF in both modes.
Covers a CENTER toggle while running, a PRESC change mid-period, a POL change while running, and a write in the same cycle as a boundary.
Covers EN/GEN clear mid-pulse (truncation allowed) and re-enable with values written while stopped.
Covers accesses to unimplemented channels or offsets, and writes to COUNT.
Each case has a defined expected output behaviour.

steps.title: Verification plan centred on the no-runt guarantee and both alignment modes
steps.goal: Define a reference model, checkers and coverage that prove the period and duty for each mode, boundary-only shadow updates while running, shadow tracking while stopped, polarity and enable behaviour, and register-bus compliance.

spec_evidence.quote: Changes written by software must never produce a truncated or runt pulse
Center-aligned: active pulse is centred in the period

done_when: A cycle-accurate reference model is specified for all NUM_CH channels.
An assertion checks that no pulse width differs from the active DUTY unless EN or GEN fell during it.
An assertion checks that pwm_out equals POL within one cycle of run going low, and that the counter and dir are 0 while stopped.
Coverage bins are defined for mode x POL x DUTY class x PRESC (0 and >0) x write-phase relative to the boundary.
A register reset and readback test covers reserved bits.

assumptions.assumed: reg_rdata is a flop loaded when reg_rd=1 and otherwise holds its value. A same-cycle write to the same address returns the pre-write value.

assumptions.topic: Prescaler structure and PRESC update timing
assumptions.assumed: Use one global 16-bit prescaler shared by all channels. It is held at 0 while GEN=0. A PRESC write takes effect immediately against the live PRESC (compare uses >= so lowering PRESC wraps at once); it is not double-buffered.

assumptions.question: In edge-aligned mode, should PERIOD=N give a period of exactly N ticks (count 0..N-1) or N+1 ticks? And what should happen when PERIOD=0?

assumptions.assumed: The counter goes up from 0 to PERIOD, then down to 0, giving 2*PERIOD ticks. The period boundary, and therefore the shadow load, occurs only at the bottom (count 0). The output is active while count > PERIOD-DUTY, so the pulse is 2*DUTY ticks wide and centred on the top of the triangle.
assumptions.question: In center-aligned mode, should the period boundary (shadow load point) be at counter bottom (0) with the pulse centred at the top, or the reverse, and should loading occur only once per period?

assumptions.assumed: POL is not double-buffered and applies on the next cycle, inverting the current output level.

assumptions.question: Is there any requirement for channels to be phase-aligned (e.g., all start together when GEN is set), or are they fully independent?
